claims.text: London's famous Chinatown is a vibrant ethnic enclave centered around Gerrard Street that is packed with Chinese restaurants, bakeries, and supermarkets.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Surprisingly, the first Chinatown in London was actually located in the Limehouse area of the East End to cater to Chinese sailors.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Much of that original Limehouse Chinatown was heavily damaged by aerial bombing during the Blitz in the Second World War.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The present Chinatown only started to be recognized as such in the 1970s, as immigrants from Hong Kong opened new restaurants in what was previously a run-down part of Soho.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, the area boasts more than 80 restaurants and is completely transformed from its past, when the street was home to brothels and a French coffee house.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: A beautiful new Chinatown gate on Wardour Street, designed in the style of the Qing dynasty by Chinese artisans, was officially opened in 2016.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: While visitors come here to enjoy the incredible Chinese culture and cuisine, it is interesting to note that the area has no museums or temples.
claims.subject: self
